tools.description:
Pretty-print a JSON string with a chosen indent size.

Returns: Pretty-printed JSON string with the requested indent, or an error message if the input is invalid.
Example input: {"text":"{\"a\":1,\"b\":[2,3]}","indent":2}
On error, includes hint: Pass valid JSON as `text` (double-quoted keys/strings, no trailing commas). `indent` is an integer between 0 and 10.

tools.name: json_validate
tools.description:
Validate a JSON string. Returns { valid, error? }.

Returns: JSON { valid: boolean, error?: string }.
Example input: {"text":"{\"a\":1}"}
On error, includes hint: Pass the JSON string as `text`.

tools.name: csv_to_json
tools.description:
Parse CSV text into JSON. Uses the first row as headers unless header=false.

Returns: JSON array of row objects keyed by the header row.
Example input: {"text":"name,age\nAda,36\nGrace,85","delimiter":","}
On error, includes hint: `text` must be CSV with a header row unless `header:false`. Escape embedded quotes as "".

header.description: First row is header (default true). If false, returns array of arrays.

tools.name: json_to_csv
tools.description:
Convert an array of JSON objects to CSV. Columns are inferred from the union of keys.

Returns: CSV string with a header row derived from the first object's keys.
Example input: {"json":"[{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"age\":36},{\"name\":\"Grace\",\"age\":85}]","delimiter":","}
On error, includes hint: `json` must be a JSON-encoded array of objects (parameter name is `json`, not `text`).

json.description: JSON array of objects, as a string.

tools.name: json_to_yaml
tools.description:
Convert a JSON string to YAML.

Returns: YAML representation of the parsed JSON value.
Example input: {"json":"{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"skills\":[\"math\",\"logic\"]}"}
On error, includes hint: Pass the JSON as `json` (a stringified JSON value), not as a JS object.

tools.name: yaml_to_json
tools.description:
Convert simple YAML (maps, lists, scalars, flow {} / []) to JSON. Anchors, tags, and complex block scalars are not supported.

Returns: Pretty-printed JSON built from the YAML input.
Example input: {"yaml":"name: Ada\nskills:\n  - math\n  - logic"}
On error, includes hint: Pass the YAML document as `yaml`; only 2-space indented block YAML is supported.

tools.name: tsv_parse
tools.description:
Parse tab-separated values into JSON. First row is treated as header unless header=false.

Returns: JSON array of row objects derived from the TSV header row.
Example input: {"text":"name\tage\nAda\t36\nGrace\t85"}
On error, includes hint: `text` must use real tab (\t) separators, not multiple spaces.

tools.name: hash
tools.description:
Compute a cryptographic hash of a string.

Returns: Hex digest of the input using the requested algorithm.
Example input: {"text":"hello world","algorithm":"sha256"}
On error, includes hint: `algorithm` must be one of: md5, sha1, sha256, sha384, sha512.

algorithm.description: md5, sha1, sha256, sha384, or sha512

tools.name: hash_compare

Hash two inputs with the same algorithm and compare them in constant time. Useful for verifying file integrity.

Returns: JSON { match: boolean } computed with a constant-time comparison.
Example input: {"a":"hello","b":"hello","algorithm":"sha256"}
On error, includes hint: `algorithm` (optional, default sha256) must be one of: md5, sha1, sha256, sha384, sha512.

tools.name: uuid_generate

tools.name: password_generate

Generate a cryptographically random password. Choose length and character classes.

Returns: Randomly generated password string.
Example input: {"length":20,"uppercase":true,"lowercase":true,"digits":true,"symbols":true,"count":1}
On error, includes hint: `length` 4-256. Enable at least one character class (lowercase/uppercase/digits/symbols).

tools.name: bcrypt_hash
tools.description:
Hash a password with bcrypt.

Returns: Bcrypt hash string (includes cost + salt).
Example input: {"password":"s3cret!","cost":10}
On error, includes hint: `cost` must be an integer between 4 and 12. Higher cost is exponentially slower.

tools.name: bcrypt_verify
tools.description:
Check whether a password matches a bcrypt hash.

Returns: JSON { match: boolean }.
Example input: {"password":"s3cret!","hash":"$2a$10$abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv"}
On error, includes hint: `hash` must be a full bcrypt string starting with $2a$, $2b$, or $2y$.

tools.name: subnet_calculator
tools.description:
Given a CIDR block (e.g. 10.0.0.0/24), return network, broadcast, netmask, first/last host, and host count.

Returns: JSON with network, broadcast, first/last host, host count, and mask for the CIDR.
Example input: {"cidr":"192.168.1.0/24"}
On error, includes hint: `cidr` must be IPv4 in `A.B.C.D/prefix` form, prefix 0-32.

tools.name: ip_convert
tools.description:
Convert an IPv4 address between dotted-decimal, integer, binary, and hex forms. Accepts any of those as input.

Returns: JSON { decimal, integer, hex, binary } representations of the IPv4 address.
Example input: {"value":"192.168.1.1"}
On error, includes hint: `value` accepts dotted (192.168.0.1), integer (3232235521), 32-bit binary, or 0x-prefixed hex.

value.description: IPv4 in dotted (192.168.0.1), integer (3232235521), binary (32 bits), or hex (0xC0A80001) form.

tools.name: epoch_convert
tools.description:
Convert between Unix epoch seconds/milliseconds and ISO 8601. Pass a number to convert to ISO, or an ISO string to convert to epoch.

Returns: JSON with ISO string, epoch seconds, epoch milliseconds, and a UTC-formatted representation.
Example input: {"value":"1700000000"}
On error, includes hint: `value` is a string: either an integer (seconds or ms since epoch) or an ISO 8601 timestamp.

value.description: A number (as string) or an ISO 8601 date string.

tools.name: timezone_convert
tools.description:
Convert a timestamp between two IANA timezones. Returns the wall-clock time in the target zone.

Returns: JSON { utc, zone, local } with the timestamp rendered in the target IANA timezone.
Example input: {"timestamp":"2026-07-11T12:00:00Z","to":"America/Los_Angeles"}
On error, includes hint: `timestamp` must be ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-07-11T12:00:00Z); `to` must be an IANA zone like America/New_York.

tools.name: date_diff
tools.description:
Compute the difference between two ISO 8601 timestamps in days, hours, minutes, and seconds.

Returns: JSON with milliseconds, totalSeconds/Minutes/Hours/Days, and a { days, hours, minutes, seconds } breakdown.
Example input: {"from":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-07-11T12:00:00Z"}
On error, includes hint: Both `from` and `to` must be ISO 8601 timestamps.

tools.name: cron_validate

On error, includes hint: `expression` must be a 5-field cron (minute hour dom month dow). 6-field / Quartz syntax is not supported.

tools.name: regex_test

On error, includes hint: `pattern` is a JS RegExp source (double-escape backslashes in JSON). `flags` uses standard flags like g, i, m, s.

Example input: {"color":"#3b82f6"}
On error, includes hint: `color` accepts #rgb, #rrggbb, rgb(r,g,b), or hsl(h,s%,l%).

color.description: Color in hex, rgb(), or hsl() form.

On error, includes hint: Both colors must be hex (#rgb or #rrggbb).

stops.description: Color stops, e.g. ['#3B82F6', '#8B5CF6 50%', '#EC4899'] — hex, rgb(), hsl(), or named colors, with optional percentage.

tools.name: avro_check
tools.description:
Validate an Avro schema against the Apache Avro 1.11 specification: names, unions, defaults, enums and fixed sizes, each fault reported at its path. Optionally check a datum (in plain JSON form) against the schema too.

Returns: JSON { valid, type?, errors[], datum?{ valid, errors[], warnings[] } }.
Example input: {"text":"{\"type\":\"record\",\"name\":\"User\",\"fields\":[{\"name\":\"id\",\"type\":\"long\"}]}"}
On error, includes hint: The schema must be JSON. A datum is given in plain JSON form: a union value directly, not wrapped like Avro's JSON encoding.

datum.description: A value to validate against the schema, as plain JSON (a union value given directly, not wrapped).

tools.name: cbor_decode
tools.description:
Decode CBOR (RFC 8949) to JSON: definite and indefinite lengths, half/single/double floats, bignums as {$int64}, byte strings as {$bytes, hex}, tags as {$tag} with datetime tags 0 and 1 rendered as ISO-8601, simple values and undefined kept visible, non-string map keys preserved as $key entries. Decodes the RFC's own appendix-A vectors exactly.

Returns: JSON { value, trailingBytes } — value uses $int64/$bytes/$tag/$simple/$undefined tags where plain JSON cannot carry the original.
Example input: {"data":"a26161016162820203"}
On error, includes hint: An RFC 8949 appendix-A vector: {"a": 1, "b": [2, 3]}.

data.description: The CBOR bytes, hex or base64.

tools.name: chmod_convert
tools.description:
Convert Unix permissions between octal (755, 4755), symbolic (rwxr-xr-x) and ls -l strings, or apply a chmod expression such as 'go-w,u+x' to a starting mode. Explains each class, setuid/setgid/sticky bits and risky modes, and gives umask defaults.

Returns: JSON { octal, symbolic, ls, description[], warnings[], command, symbolicArg, umaskDefaults{ umask, newFile, newDirectory } }.
Example input: {"mode":"rwxr-x---"}
On error, includes hint: Use 1-4 octal digits, nine rwx characters (optionally with a leading file type), or a symbolic expression like u+x,go-w.

mode.description: Octal (644), symbolic or ls -l (-rwsr-xr-x), or a chmod expression (u+x, a=rX) applied to start.

start.description: Starting octal mode for expressions. Default 644 for files, 755 for directories.

isDirectory.description: Treat the target as a directory (affects X and the ls -l type). Default false.

umask.description: umask in octal, used for expressions without u/g/o/a and for new-file defaults. Default 022.

tools.name: gc_log_analyze
tools.description:
Analyze a JVM garbage-collection log (JDK 9+ unified -Xlog:gc* or JDK 8 -XX:+PrintGCDetails): pause count and percentiles by type, Full GC count, throughput over the log span, allocation-rate estimate, heap reclaimed, and the warning signs (to-space exhausted, Metadata GC Threshold, promotion failure, Full GCs more than once a minute).

Returns: The text summary plus structured figures: collections, fulls, span, throughput, pause percentiles (ms), allocation rate, warnings.
Example input: {"text":"[0.017s][info][gc] GC(0) Pause Young (Normal) (G1 Evacuation Pause) 23M->3M(64M) 0.720ms\n[1.478s][info][gc] GC(16) Pause Full (System.gc()) 35M->8M(34M) 4.797ms\n"}
On error, includes hint: Throughput is only meaningful when the log spans at least a few seconds; the summary withholds it below 5s rather than print noise.

tools.name: json_tree
tools.description:
Draw JSON as a box-drawing tree: one line per key or array index, with value previews and item counts, so the shape of a payload is readable without counting brackets. Long string values are cut in the preview; the counts stay exact.

Returns: The tree as plain text, drawn with ├─ and └─ branches.
Example input: {"text":"{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"tags\":[\"math\",\"code\"]}"}
On error, includes hint: Any valid JSON document works, including a bare number or string.

tools.name: jvm_thread_dump
tools.description:
Analyze a jstack / jcmd Thread.print dump: thread states, pools, lock contention, identical stacks, CPU time, and deadlocks found from the lock graph itself (knowing Object.wait() releases its monitor). Returns the verdict-first text summary plus the structured analysis.

Returns: The text summary (verdict first: deadlocks, then states, contention, pools, identical stacks, CPU), plus structured counts.
Example input: {"text":"\"main\" #1 prio=5 os_prio=31 cpu=29.70ms elapsed=3.18s tid=0x0001 nid=0x2703 waiting on condition  [0x0001]\n   java.lang.Thread.State: TIMED_WAITING (sleeping)\n\tat java.lang.Thread.sleep(Native Method)\n\tat Main.main(Main.java:19)\n"}
On error, includes hint: Paste the whole dump, including the 'Found one Java-level deadlock' section when present; deadlocks are also derived independently from - locked / - waiting to lock lines.

text.description: The thread dump text (jstack, jcmd Thread.print, or a SIGQUIT print).

tools.name: msgpack_decode
tools.description:
Decode MessagePack bytes to JSON, with the lossy edges tagged instead of silently coerced: 64-bit integers past 2^53 as {$int64}, binary as {$bytes, hex}, extensions as {$ext}, the timestamp extension as ISO-8601, non-string map keys preserved as $key entries. Trailing bytes after the first value are reported.

Returns: JSON { value, trailingBytes } — value uses $int64/$bytes/$ext/$timestamp tags where plain JSON cannot carry the original.
Example input: {"data":"82a7636f6d70616374c3a6736368656d6100"}
On error, includes hint: The msgpack.org homepage document: {"compact":true,"schema":0}.

data.description: The MessagePack bytes, hex or base64.

tools.name: proto_decode
tools.description:
Decode protobuf wire format without a schema: field numbers, wire types and values, nested messages detected by trial decode. Length-delimited fields are genuinely ambiguous without the .proto (string vs bytes vs message vs packed), so every reading that fits is shown — varints as both unsigned and zigzag — rather than one guess.

Returns: One line per field: number, wire type, value(s); nested decodes indented, with the alternative text reading noted when both fit.
Example input: {"data":"089601120774657374696e67"}
On error, includes hint: Field 1 varint 150 then field 2 string "testing" — the examples from the protobuf encoding guide.

data.description: The message bytes, hex or base64.

tools.name: xml_tree
tools.description:
Outline an XML document's element tree with attribute counts, child counts and text previews, leaving out the closing-tag noise. Mismatched or unclosed tags are reported by name instead of being guessed around.

Returns: The element outline as plain text, drawn with ├─ and └─ branches.
Example input: {"text":"<order id=\"7\"><item sku=\"a-1\">Widget</item></order>"}
On error, includes hint: Comments, DOCTYPE and the XML declaration are skipped; elements, attributes and text are shown.

tools.name: color_palette
tools.description:
Build a harmonious color palette from one base color (complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary, tetradic, square, monochromatic or tints and shades). Returns each color as HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH with WCAG contrast against white and black, an 11-step 50-950 scale of the base, and ready-to-paste CSS variables and Tailwind config. Same maths as https://redbison.dev/color-palette-generator.

Returns: JSON { base, rule, wheel, colors[] { role, hex, rgb, hsl, oklch, contrastOnWhite, contrastOnBlack, bestTextColor, wcagNormalText }, scale { '50'..'950': hex }, baseScaleStep, css, tailwindV3, tailwindV4 }.
Example input: {"base":"#3b82f6","rule":"triadic","wheel":"rgb","name":"brand"}
On error, includes hint: Pass the base color as hex like #3b82f6 (rgb(), hsl(), oklch() and CSS names also work). rule must be one of complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary, tetradic, square, monochromatic, shades.

base.description: Base color as hex (#3b82f6), rgb(59 130 246), hsl(217 91% 60%), oklch(62% 0.19 260) or a CSS color name.

wheel.description: Color wheel for hue rotation: 'rgb' (screen/HSL wheel, default), 'ryb' (approximate painter's wheel, red opposite green) or 'oklch' (perceptual, keeps lightness).

name.description: Name used in the CSS and Tailwind exports, e.g. 'brand'. Default 'brand'.

tools.name: cron_build
tools.description:
Build a standard five-field cron expression from plain choices (every N minutes, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly) or explain an existing one. Returns the expression, an English description, the next run times in a time zone, and the same schedule for crontab, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Quartz and AWS EventBridge.

Returns: JSON { expression, description, nextRuns[], timezone, platforms[{ id, name, value, notes[] }], warnings[] }. value is null on Quartz/EventBridge when both day fields are restricted.
Example input: {"frequency":"weekly","daysOfWeek":["mon","wed","fri"],"hours":[9],"minute":30,"timezone":"America/New_York"}
On error, includes hint: Give either plain choices (frequency plus minute/hours/days) or a five-field expression. Days of week accept names or 0-6 with 0 = Sunday.

frequency.description: How often to run. Ignored when expression is given. Default daily.

interval.description: For minutes: every N minutes (default 5). For hourly: every N hours (default 1).

hours.description: Hours of the day in 24-hour time, e.g. [9] or [9, 17]. Default [0].

daysOfWeek.description: For weekly: days as names (mon, fri) or numbers 0-6 with 0 = Sunday.

daysOfMonth.description: For monthly or yearly: days of the month, e.g. [1, 15].

expression.description: An existing five-field cron expression to explain and translate instead of building one.

timezone.description: IANA time zone for the next run times, e.g. Europe/London. Default UTC.

count.description: How many upcoming runs to list. Default 5.

tools.name: css_beautify
tools.description:
Pretty-print or minify CSS, SCSS or Less, optionally sorting declarations alphabetically. Sorting is cascade-safe: a shorthand and its longhands (border / border-top, margin / margin-top, font / line-height) keep their original relative order. Minify removes comments and whitespace only; values such as 0px or colours are never rewritten.

Returns: Text: the stylesheet. structuredContent { code, movedDeclarations, warnings[] }.
Example input: {"css":".a{z-index:1;color:red;border-top:1px solid;border:0}","mode":"beautify","syntax":"css","sort":true,"indent":2}
On error, includes hint: Unbalanced braces or an unterminated string or comment are reported as errors.

mode.description: beautify = one declaration per line, minify = smallest output.

syntax.description: Input syntax; scss and less also accept // line comments.

sort.description: Sort declarations inside each rule alphabetically (vendor-prefixed copies first, override pairs kept in order).

indent.description: Spaces per indent level when beautifying (0 = tabs).

tools.name: curl_to_code
tools.description:
Convert a curl command (bash/zsh quoting, $'...' strings, \ line continuations, or Windows cmd ^ escaping from 'Copy as cURL') into JavaScript fetch, Node Axios, Python requests, Go net/http or PHP ext-curl. Follows curl semantics: -d implies POST with application/x-www-form-urlencoded, repeated -d joins with &, --json sets JSON headers, -G moves data to the query string, -F is multipart, -u is Basic auth, no redirects without -L. Nothing is sent over the network.

Returns: Text: the generated code, followed by notes on anything not translated. structuredContent { code, method, url, headers[{ name, value }], hasBody, warnings[] }.
Example input: {"command":"curl -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/items -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"name\":\"Ada\"}'","target":"python"}
On error, includes hint: Send the command exactly as copied, including quotes. The word curl must be present.

tools.name: docker_run_to_compose
tools.description:
Convert one or more 'docker run' commands into a Compose file (services, ports, volumes, environment, networks, healthcheck, GPUs, limits), or convert a compose.yaml back into docker run commands. Unsupported flags are reported as warnings.

Returns: run_to_compose: JSON { compose (YAML text), services[], warnings[] }. compose_to_run: JSON { commands[], warnings[] }.
Example input: {"input":"docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 -v html:/usr/share/nginx/html --restart unless-stopped nginx:alpine"}
On error, includes hint: Each command must start with 'docker run' (or 'docker container run'). Separate several commands with new lines.

input.description: docker run command(s), or compose YAML when direction is compose_to_run.

project.description: Compose project name used to prefix volume and network names in compose_to_run. Default myproject.

tools.name: gitignore_generate

extra.description: Extra lines to append, one pattern per line.

testPaths.description: Repository-relative paths to check, e.g. ['.env', 'dist/']. End with / for a directory.

tools.name: hmac
tools.description:
Compute an HMAC (RFC 2104) with SHA-256, SHA-1, SHA-384 or SHA-512 and return it in hex, Base64 and Base64url. Optionally build a GitHub, Stripe or Slack webhook signature, and check an expected signature with a constant-time comparison.

Returns: JSON { algorithm, hex, base64, base64url, bits, key_bytes, message_bytes, signed_string, header, match } where match is null unless `expected` was given.
Example input: {"message":"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog","key":"key","algorithm":"SHA-256"}
On error, includes hint: `algorithm` is SHA-256, SHA-1, SHA-384 or SHA-512; `key_encoding` and `message_encoding` are utf8, hex or base64; `preset` is plain, github, stripe or slack.

message.description: The message or raw request body to sign.

algorithm.description: Hash function (default SHA-256). Webhook presets always use SHA-256.

key_encoding.description: How the key is written (default utf8).

message_encoding.description: How the message is written (default utf8). Ignored for webhook presets.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp used by the stripe and slack presets.

expected.description: Optional signature to verify, in hex or Base64, with or without a sha256= / v0= / v1= prefix.

tools.name: http_status

query.description: A status code such as 429, a class such as 3xx, or search words such as 'redirect keep method'.

includeUnofficial.description: Include vendor codes such as nginx 499 and Cloudflare 522. Default true.

tools.name: js_beautify
tools.description:
Format JavaScript, TypeScript or JSX with js-beautify, or minify JavaScript/TypeScript by removing comments and whitespace (no renaming, no rewriting; line breaks are kept where automatic semicolon insertion needs them). The output is re-lexed and compared token by token with the input.

Returns: Text: the formatted or minified code. structuredContent { code, mode, inputBytes, outputBytes, savedPercent, warnings[] }.
Example input: {"code":"function add(a,b){return a+b}","mode":"beautify","language":"javascript","indent":2,"brace_style":"collapse","keep_license":true}
On error, includes hint: Pass the whole file as `code`. An unterminated string, comment or regex is reported with its line and column.

code.description: Source code to format or minify.

mode.description: beautify = pretty-print, minify = strip comments and whitespace.

language.description: Language of the code. TypeScript gets generic and optional-marker fix-ups; JSX cannot be minified.

indent.description: Spaces per indent level when beautifying (0 = tabs).

brace_style.description: Brace placement when beautifying: collapse = K&R (same line), expand = Allman (own line).

tools.name: json_schema_validate
tools.description:
Validate a JSON document against a JSON Schema (drafts 06, 07, 2019-09 and 2020-12, via Ajv, all errors reported with JSON Pointer paths and formats such as date-time, email, uuid, ipv4/ipv6 checked), or infer a starter schema from sample JSON. Leave `schema` empty to infer.

Returns: Validate: text summary plus structuredContent { mode, valid, draft, errors[{ path, message, keyword, schemaPath, params }], warnings[] }. Infer: the schema as JSON text and structuredContent { mode, schema }.
Example input: {"data":"{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"age\":-1}","schema":"{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"age\":{\"type\":\"integer\",\"minimum\":0}},\"required\":[\"name\",\"email\"]}","draft":"auto"}
On error, includes hint: Both `data` and `schema` are JSON text, not objects. Send an empty `schema` to generate one from `data`.

data.description: The JSON document (as text) to validate, or the sample to infer a schema from.

schema.description: The JSON Schema as text. Empty = infer a schema from `data` instead of validating.

draft.description: Draft for validation; auto reads $schema and defaults to 2020-12.

infer_draft.description: Draft of the generated schema when inferring.

infer_required.description: When inferring: all = keys present in every sampled object are required.

tools.name: markdown_table
tools.description:
Turn CSV, TSV (spreadsheet paste) or an existing Markdown table into a GitHub Flavored Markdown table. The first row is the header; pipes are escaped as \|, line breaks inside cells become
, and columns can be padded so the pipes line up (CJK-width aware). Returns: Text: the Markdown table. structuredContent { markdown, rows (including header), columns, detected ('csv' | 'tsv' | 'markdown' | 'other'), errors[] }. Example input: {"text":"Item,Qty,Price\nApple,3,$1.20\nKiwi,12,$0.50","align":"none","pretty":true,"outer_pipes":true,"bold_header":false} On error, includes hint: Put the header in the first row. Quote CSV fields that contain commas or line breaks.

text.description: CSV, TSV or Markdown table text. The delimiter is detected automatically.

align.description: Alignment for every column (none keeps alignment from a Markdown input).

pretty.description: Pad cells so the columns line up in plain text.

outer_pipes.description: Start and end each row with |.

tools.name: mime_lookup

query.description: An extension (webp or .webp), a file name (report.docx, archive.tar.gz) or a MIME type (application/json, image/*).

tools.name: morse_code

input.description: Text to encode, or Morse to decode (dots and dashes; '/' or two spaces between words).

direction.description: auto decodes when the input contains only dots, dashes, slashes and spaces.

wpm.description: Character speed in words per minute (PARIS standard) for the timing figures.

effectiveWpm.description: Farnsworth overall speed in wpm, lower than wpm. Omit for standard spacing.

tools.name: nato_phonetic

text.description: Text to spell, or code words to decode (e.g. 'Alfa Bravo / Charlie').

direction.description: spell turns text into code words; decode turns code words back into text.

spelling.description: icao prints Alfa and Juliett as published; common prints Alpha and Juliet.

digits.description: icao says Tree, Fower, Fife, Niner; plain says Three, Four, Five, Nine.

markCase.description: Prefix each letter with Capital or Lowercase.

tools.name: password_strength
tools.description:
Estimate how guessable a password is with zxcvbn pattern matching (dictionary words, common passwords, keyboard walks, sequences, dates, l33t). Returns a 0-4 score, estimated guesses, entropy in bits, crack times for online and offline attacks, warnings, suggestions and NIST SP 800-63B-4 length checks. The password is not echoed back.

Returns: JSON { score 0-4, label, length, guesses, guesses_log10, entropy_bits, character_pool_entropy_bits, character_classes[], crack_times[{scenario, seconds, display}], warning, suggestions[], patterns[{pattern, start, end, description}], nist_sp800_63b{...} }. The password itself is never included.
Example input: {"password":"Tr0ub4dor&3","user_inputs":["alice"]}
On error, includes hint: `password` must be a string of at most 256 characters; `user_inputs` is an optional array of strings.

password.description: The password to analyse (up to 256 characters).

user_inputs.description: Optional personal words (name, username, site name) that make the password easier to guess if it contains them.

tools.name: readability

text.description: English text to score. 100+ words gives stable results; SMOG expects 30 sentences.

lineBreaksEndSentences.description: Treat each line break as a sentence end (true for headings and lists; false for hard-wrapped plain text).

maxSentences.description: How many hard sentences to list, hardest first.

tools.name: redirect_rules

rules.description: One redirect per line: '/old /new', '/old /new 302' or '/blog/* /news/:splat'. Destinations may be absolute URLs.

defaultCode.description: Status code for lines without one. Default 301.

keepQuery.description: Keep the incoming query string. Default true.

forceHttps.description: Add an HTTP to HTTPS redirect (Apache, nginx).

canonicalHost.description: Redirect the other host variant to www or to the bare domain.

domain.description: Apex domain for host rules, e.g. example.com.

tools.name: toml_convert
tools.description:
Convert between TOML 1.0, JSON and YAML, validating the input. TOML dates become RFC 3339 strings in JSON; nulls are dropped when writing TOML (it has no null) and reported; integers beyond 2^53 are kept exact; inf and nan become strings in JSON. Use from=toml,to=toml to validate and normalise a TOML file.

Returns: Text: the converted document. structuredContent { output, warnings[] } where warnings list dropped nulls, large integers and non-finite numbers.
Example input: {"text":"[package]
name = "demo"
version = "0.1.0"

[dependencies]
serde = "1.0"","from":"toml","to":"json","indent":2}
On error, includes hint: TOML output needs an object at the top level; wrap arrays in a key.

indent.description: Indent for JSON and YAML output.

detect_dates.description: When writing TOML, turn RFC 3339 date/date-time strings into native TOML dates.

tools.name: user_agent_parse
utm_build

url.description: Landing page URL. https:// is added if the scheme is missing.

source.description: utm_source: who sends the traffic, e.g. newsletter, linkedin, google.

medium.description: utm_medium: marketing medium, e.g. email, social, cpc, referral, affiliate.

campaign.description: utm_campaign: campaign, product or promotion name.

id.description: utm_id: campaign ID used for GA4 data import.

content.description: utm_content: which link or creative, e.g. header_button.

lowercase.description: Lowercase every value (default true; GA4 values are case sensitive).

spaces.description: How to write spaces inside values: dash (default), underscore, plus (+) or keep (%20).

tools.name: word_count

readingWpm.description: Silent reading speed in words per minute (238 is the adult non-fiction average).

speakingWpm.description: Speaking speed in words per minute for the speech-time estimate.

topWords.description: How many frequent words to return, stop words excluded. 0 to skip.

tools.name: number_base_convert
tools.description:
Convert a number between binary, octal, decimal, hex and any base from 2 to 36, with arbitrary-size integers (BigInt), exact fractional parts (repeating digits in parentheses, e.g. 0.1 decimal = 0.0(0011) binary) and an optional two's complement view at a chosen bit width with signed/unsigned readings and big- and little-endian bytes.

Returns: JSON { fromBase, fraction, binary, octal, decimal, hex, target{ base, value }|null, bitLength, twosComplement{ width, binary, hex, signed, unsigned, bytesBigEndian, bytesLittleEndian, overflow, min, max, maxUnsigned }|null, warnings[] }.
Example input: {"value":"-42","width":16}
On error, includes hint: Digits must be valid in the base (0-9 then a-z). Two's complement needs a whole number and a width; set inputIsPattern to read hex like FFD6 as a signed value.

value.description: The number. Accepts a sign, 0x/0o/0b prefixes, '_' separators and a fractional part, e.g. '255', '-42', '0xFF', '10.625'.

from.description: Base of the input, 2 to 36. Omit to read it from a 0x/0o/0b prefix, otherwise decimal.

to.description: An extra target base besides 2, 8, 10 and 16.

width.description: Bit width for the two's complement view (8, 16, 32, 64 or any 1-1024).

inputIsPattern.description: Read the input as a two's complement bit pattern of `width` bits, so FF at 8 bits is -1. Default false.

tools.name: ieee754_float
tools.description:
Encode a decimal (0.1, 6.02e23), exact fraction (1/3), hex float (0x1.8p3), inf or nan into IEEE 754-2019 binary16, binary32 or binary64 with round-to-nearest-even, or decode a hex or binary bit pattern. Returns sign, exponent and fraction bits, the class (normal, subnormal, zero, infinity, NaN with payload), the exact decimal value stored, the shortest round-trip decimal, the rounding error, nextUp/nextDown and the bytes in both byte orders.

Returns: JSON { format, bits, hex, bytesBigEndian, bytesLittleEndian, sign, exponentBits, fractionBits, biasedExponent, exponent, class, formula, exactValue, shortest, ulp, nextUp{ hex, value }, nextDown{ hex, value }, nan{ quiet, payload, payloadHex }|null, rounding{ input, exact, error, relativeError, overflow, underflow }|null }.
Example input: {"value":"0.1","format":"binary32"}
On error, includes hint: Encode accepts decimals, p/q fractions, C hex floats, inf and nan. Decode takes up to the format's width in big-endian order: 4, 8 or 16 hex digits, or a 0b-prefixed binary pattern (unprefixed binary must be exactly 16, 32 or 64 digits).

value.description: A number to encode, or a bit pattern to decode (hex such as 3DCCCCCD or 0x3FB999999999999A, or binary).

format.description: binary16 (half), binary32 (float, single) or binary64 (double). Default binary32.

mode.description: encode a number (default) or decode a bit pattern.

tools.name: dice_roll
tools.description:
Roll dice from standard notation (3d6+2, d20, d%, 4d6kh3 keep highest, 2d20kl1 keep lowest, 4d6dl1 drop lowest, 1d8+1d6-1) with crypto-random, unbiased dice, and get the exact odds: average, standard deviation, most likely totals and, optionally, the chance of every total counted over all face combinations.

Returns: JSON { notation, min, max, rolls[{ total, detail }], odds{ outcomes, mean, sd, mostLikely[], median, table?[{ total, ways, p, atLeast, atMost }], tableNote? }|null }. table is given for up to 1,000 possible totals; above that tableNote explains why it is missing. Dropped dice appear in parentheses in detail; odds is null when the expression has too many combinations to count.
Example input: {"notation":"4d6kh3","rolls":0}
On error, includes hint: Join terms with + or -; keep with kh/kl (4d6kh3), drop with dl/dh (4d6dl1). Set rolls to 0 for odds only and table to true for every total.

notation.description: Dice notation, e.g. '3d6+2', '4d6kh3', '2d20kl1'. Up to 100 dice with 2 to 1000 sides.

rolls.description: How many times to roll (default 1; 0 = odds only).

table.description: Include the chance of every total (exactly, at least, at most), for expressions with up to 1,000 possible totals. Default false.

tools.name: tournament_bracket
tools.description:
Build a seeded single or double elimination bracket (padded to the next power of two, byes to the top seeds, standard 1 v n seeding) or a round robin schedule by the circle method. Players are given in seed order. Returns the round-one pairings, byes, every round and a printable text version.

Returns: Elimination: JSON { format, players, bracketSize, byes, gamesNeeded{ min, max }, rounds[{ name, matches[{ id, top, bottom, walkover }] }], text }. Round robin: { format, players, rounds[{ round, games[[a, b]], sitsOut }], games, text }. Later-round slots read TBD.
Example input: {"players":["Alder","Birch","Cedar","Hazel","Maple","Rowan"],"format":"single"}
On error, includes hint: List players strongest first; pass format 'double' for a losers bracket or 'round-robin' for everyone-plays-everyone. Shuffle the list yourself for random seeding.

players.description: Player or team names in seed order (seed 1 first). Names must be unique.

tools.name: would_you_rather
tools.description:
Draw random would-you-rather questions from RedBison's original question bank, filtered by audience (kids, family, work, party), with no repeats within one call.

Returns: JSON { audience[], available, questions[{ id, question, a, b, tags[] }] }.
Example input: {"audience":["work"],"count":3}
On error, includes hint: Audiences: kids, family, work, party. count is capped at the number of matching questions.

audience.description: Audiences to include; a question tagged with any of them qualifies. Omit for all.

count.description: How many questions (default 5, capped at the number available).

tools.name: military_time_convert

time.description: The time to convert, e.g. '1430', '09:30' or '2:30 PM'.

direction.description: toCivilian: 24-hour in, AM/PM out; toMilitary: AM/PM in, 24-hour out.

tools.name: number_to_words

value.description: The number, e.g. '1234.56' or '-17'. Commas are allowed.

tools.name: binary_text_convert

input.description: Text to encode, or bits/bytes to decode.

tools.name: css_color_convert
paper_size_lookup

size.description: The paper size name, e.g. 'A4' or 'Letter'.

tools.name: ring_size_convert

us.description: US ring size, 3 to 13 in halves (used when diameterMm is absent).

tools.name: help

tool.description: Tool name, e.g. 'run_calculator', 'hash' or 'list_calculators'. Omit to list all tools.

calculator.description: With tool 'run_calculator': a calculator id such as 'mortgage-calculator' for its inputs and a worked sample.
